title: How Spotify Really Makes Money (And Why It Lost Money for Years)
description:
Spotify has almost 790 million users and more than 300 million paying subscribers — yet for most of its life it lost money, because about 70% of what it earns goes straight to the music industry. In this file we open the money machine behind Spotify: two Swedes and a piracy problem, the freemium model, where your monthly payment really goes, the $10 billion a year paid to music, the podcast and audiobook escape plan, the long road from losses to profit, the tiny 2025 tax bill, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Spotify quarterly results (Q4 2025 and Q3 2026 reports, SEC Form 6-K); Spotify newsroom; Music Business Worldwide; Hypebot; Complete Music Update; Europa Press / La Nación; The Irish Times; CNBC; TechCrunch; Gizmodo; Wikipedia (Spotify, Martin Lorentzon).

All figures are rounded. The ~89% Premium share of 2025 revenue is our own arithmetic from reported figures. The ~70% rights-holder share is an approximate public estimate. Joe Rogan deal values are press reports, not company figures. Q4 2026 operating profit is company guidance. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
